decks.domain: Night driving, defensive observation and sight distance

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Watch for large trucks and underpowered cars losing speed on steep grades or ____.
cards.back: Watch for large trucks and underpowered cars losing speed on steep grades or taking longer to accelerate into traffic.
cards.memory_hook: taking longer to accelerate into traffic

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles commonly travel at twenty-five ____.
cards.back: Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles commonly travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less.
cards.memory_hook: miles per hour or less

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The handbook says these slow vehicles should carry an orange triangular ____.
cards.back: The handbook says these slow vehicles should carry an orange triangular slow-moving-vehicle emblem at the rear.
cards.memory_hook: slow-moving-vehicle emblem at the rear

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Reduce speed in crowded places where maneuvering ____.
cards.back: Reduce speed in crowded places where maneuvering room is limited.
cards.memory_hook: room is limited

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Shopping areas, parking lots and downtown streets can require lower speeds because vehicles and ____.
cards.back: Shopping areas, parking lots and downtown streets can require lower speeds because vehicles and pedestrians move unpredictably in several directions.
cards.memory_hook: pedestrians move unpredictably in several directions

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Rush-hour congestion and hurried drivers are reasons ____.
cards.back: Rush-hour congestion and hurried drivers are reasons to consider slowing.
cards.memory_hook: to consider slowing

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Narrow bridges and tunnels may require slower travel because opposing ____.
cards.back: Narrow bridges and tunnels may require slower travel because opposing vehicles pass closer together.
cards.memory_hook: vehicles pass closer together

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: At toll plazas, watch for lane changes, stops and acceleration, and for the ____.
cards.back: At toll plazas, watch for lane changes, stops and acceleration, and for the lane count changing on either side.
cards.memory_hook: lane count changing on either side

decks.domain: Night driving, defensive observation and sight distance

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, remain ready for children ____.
cards.back: Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, remain ready for children entering the roadway without looking.
cards.memory_hook: entering the roadway without looking

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: At railroad crossings, check for trains and space beyond the tracks, slow for rough ____.
cards.back: At railroad crossings, check for trains and space beyond the tracks, slow for rough crossings and avoid blocking the tracks.
cards.memory_hook: crossings and avoid blocking the tracks

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Nighttime reduces how far and how readily a driver can detect objects, ____.
cards.back: Nighttime reduces how far and how readily a driver can detect objects, and familiar surroundings can appear different.
cards.memory_hook: and familiar surroundings can appear different

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Approaching-headlight glare can impair vision while the eyes ____.
cards.back: Approaching-headlight glare can impair vision while the eyes readjust to lower light.
cards.memory_hook: readjust to lower light

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Avoid outdriving the headlights by choosing a speed that permits stopping ____.
cards.back: Avoid outdriving the headlights by choosing a speed that permits stopping within the visible roadway ahead.
cards.memory_hook: within the visible roadway ahead

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: When meeting vehicles at night, use brief glances to judge their lane position ____.
cards.back: When meeting vehicles at night, use brief glances to judge their lane position rather than staring into their headlights.
cards.memory_hook: rather than staring into their headlights

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: At night, use quick checks to maintain your position and ____.
cards.back: At night, use quick checks to maintain your position and identify the road’s right edge.
cards.memory_hook: identify the road’s right edge

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Continue looking ahead for objects in the vehicle’s path ____.
cards.back: Continue looking ahead for objects in the vehicle’s path while managing nighttime glare.
cards.memory_hook: while managing nighttime glare

decks.domain: Night driving, defensive observation and sight distance

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Do not assume a flashing turn signal guarantees a turn; plan for the ____.
cards.back: Do not assume a flashing turn signal guarantees a turn; plan for the other driver either turning or continuing.
cards.memory_hook: other driver either turning or continuing

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Do not assume every driver will obey a stop ____.
cards.back: Do not assume every driver will obey a stop sign or red signal.
cards.memory_hook: sign or red signal

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Continually consider an escape route and note the shoulder and surrounding ____.
cards.back: Continually consider an escape route and note the shoulder and surrounding area before an emergency occurs.
cards.memory_hook: area before an emergency occurs

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: If an opposing vehicle begins passing without apparent room, slow down and be prepared to use a ____.
cards.back: If an opposing vehicle begins passing without apparent room, slow down and be prepared to use a previously identified escape route if necessary.
cards.memory_hook: previously identified escape route if necessary

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: With good tires and brakes on dry pavement, the handbook estimates that reacting and stopping from fifty miles per hour ____.
cards.back: With good tires and brakes on dry pavement, the handbook estimates that reacting and stopping from fifty miles per hour can require about four hundred feet.
cards.memory_hook: can require about four hundred feet

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Under the stated good-tire, good-brake and dry-pavement conditions, the handbook gives about two hundred feet as a stopping ____.
cards.back: Under the stated good-tire, good-brake and dry-pavement conditions, the handbook gives about two hundred feet as a stopping example at thirty miles per hour
cards.memory_hook: example at thirty miles per hour

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: If sight distance is below the stopping example for a given speed, there may be insufficient time to avoid ____.
cards.back: If sight distance is below the stopping example for a given speed, there may be insufficient time to avoid an object once it becomes visible.
cards.memory_hook: an object once it becomes visible

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: At night, travel slowly enough to stop within the distance ____.
cards.back: At night, travel slowly enough to stop within the distance illuminated by the headlights.
cards.memory_hook: illuminated by the headlights

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The handbook says visibility limited to about two hundred feet or less in heavy rain, snow or fog does not support ____.
cards.back: The handbook says visibility limited to about two hundred feet or less in heavy rain, snow or fog does not support speeds above thirty miles per hour
cards.memory_hook: speeds above thirty miles per hour

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: If rain becomes too heavy to see well enough to drive, pull off in a safe place ____.
cards.back: If rain becomes too heavy to see well enough to drive, pull off in a safe place and wait for it to clear.
cards.memory_hook: and wait for it to clear

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Slow for a hill or curve that hides the roadway so a stop ____.
cards.back: Slow for a hill or curve that hides the roadway so a stop remains possible for an unseen obstruction.
cards.memory_hook: remains possible for an unseen obstruction

decks.module: Parked vehicles, visibility and time-distance checks
decks.domain: Night driving, defensive observation and sight distance

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Give parked vehicles as much safe clearance as possible because they obscure ____.
cards.back: Give parked vehicles as much safe clearance as possible because they obscure people exiting or walking between them.
cards.memory_hook: people exiting or walking between them

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The four-second sight-distance rule checks whether vehicle speed is too high for how ____.
cards.back: The four-second sight-distance rule checks whether vehicle speed is too high for how far ahead the driver can see.
cards.memory_hook: far ahead the driver can see

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Choose a stationary object at the farthest clearly visible point and count ____.
cards.back: Choose a stationary object at the farthest clearly visible point and count four seconds while approaching it.
cards.memory_hook: four seconds while approaching it

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: If you reach the sight-distance marker before four seconds have elapsed, slow down because speed is ____.
cards.back: If you reach the sight-distance marker before four seconds have elapsed, slow down because speed is too high for the visible distance.
cards.memory_hook: too high for the visible distance

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Use the four-second sight-distance check at night to ____.
cards.back: Use the four-second sight-distance check at night to avoid outdriving the headlights.
cards.memory_hook: avoid outdriving the headlights

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Obey speed limits because they reflect road design, vehicle use and hidden entry ____.
cards.back: Obey speed limits because they reflect road design, vehicle use and hidden entry points as well as traffic volume.
cards.memory_hook: points as well as traffic volume

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Posted limits assume ideal conditions; wet or icy pavement, poor vision or heavy ____.
cards.back: Posted limits assume ideal conditions; wet or icy pavement, poor vision or heavy traffic can require a lower speed.
cards.memory_hook: traffic can require a lower speed

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: A driver can be ticketed for speed that is unsafe for conditions ____.
cards.back: A driver can be ticketed for speed that is unsafe for conditions even while below the posted limit.
cards.memory_hook: even while below the posted limit

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Maintaining space around the vehicle creates a time cushion for ____.
cards.back: Maintaining space around the vehicle creates a time cushion for reacting to other road users.
cards.memory_hook: reacting to other road users

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The three-second rule is introduced as a way to judge following distance, ____.
cards.back: The three-second rule is introduced as a way to judge following distance, distinct from the four-second sight-distance check.
cards.memory_hook: distinct from the four-second sight-distance check
